title: Mixture of Spectral Experts for Audio Deepfake Detection
authors: Yaxuan Qiu(Xinjiang University); Zhe Li(University of Hong Kong); Mieradilijiang Maimaiti(Xinjiang University); Zunwang Ke(Xinjiang University); Wushour Silamu(Xinjiang University)
session_title: Speech Deepfake Detection: Robustness, Generalization, Attribution
abstract: Recent advances in neural speech synthesis have produced highly natural waveforms, making audio deepfake detection increasingly challenging as spoofing artifacts become less perceptible. Although pre-trained speech models provide robust representations, they may overlook low-level physical cues, particularly magnitude and phase information. To address this limitation, we propose a detection framework that combines a frequency audio encoder (FAE) with spectral parameter-efficient fine-tuning. The FAE explicitly models magnitude and phase cues, while the proposed Mixture of Spectral Experts (MoSE) efficiently adapts the pre-trained speech model to generation-dependent distribution shifts. By applying low-rank updates in the singular value decomposition (SVD) domain while keeping the singular bases frozen, MoSE facilitates task-specific adaptation to spoofing-related spectral artifacts. Evaluations on ASVspoof 2019 LA, ASVspoof 2021 LA/DF, and In-the-Wild benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and its strong generalization to unseen channel variations and real-world spoofing attacks.

title: SA-HRTF: A Sound-Assisted Approach to Personalized HRTF Modeling
authors: Qingyin Zhao(Inner Mongolia University); Siyuan Chen(Inner Mongolia University); De Hu(Inner Mongolia University)
abstract: Head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) are essential for immersive binaural audio rendering, whereas generic HRTFs are often inadequate for accurately reproducing individual spatial cues. Although neural-network-based personalized HRTF modeling has progressed rapidly, accurate reconstruction under sparse measurements remains challenging because limited spatial information hinders reliable estimation. To address this issue, we propose a sound-assisted HRTF (SA-HRTF) model that incorporates binaural acoustic information into personalized HRTF estimation. The proposed architecture adopts a dual-branch design: the primary branch exploits structural features from an existing database to generate an initial estimate, while the auxiliary branch extracts perceptual cues from sound signals to provide supplementary predictions. A fusion module combines the outputs of the two branches to produce a more accurate personalized HRTF. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Explicit Context-Driven Neural Acoustic Modeling for High-Fidelity RIR Generation
authors: Chen Si(University of California San Diego); Qianyi Wu(Monash University); Chaitanya Amballa(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Romit Roy Choudhury(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)
abstract: Realistic sound simulation plays a critical role in many applications. A key element in sound simulation is the room impulse response (RIR), which characterizes how sound propagates within a given space. Recent studies have applied neural implicit methods to learn RIR using context information collected from the environment, such as scene images. However, these approaches do not effectively leverage explicit geometric information from the environment. To further exploit neural implicit models with direct geometric features, we present MiNAF, which queries a rough room mesh at given locations and extracts distance distributions as an explicit representation of local context. Our approach demonstrates that incorporating explicit local geometric features can better guide the model in generating more accurate RIR predictions. Through comparisons with conventional and state-of-the-art methods, we show that MiNAF performs competitively across various evaluation metrics.

title: Eye and Mouth Cues in Audiovisual Perception of Mandarin Irony: Evidence from Eye-tracking and Facial Masking
authors: Shifeng Xia(Nanjing University of Science and Technology); Shanpeng Li(Nanjing University of Science and Technology)
session_title: Behavioral, Cross-lingual, and Multimodal Speech Analysis
abstract: Irony is a form of nonliteral language whose comprehension involves integrating auditory and visual cues. Although prosodic cues have been widely studied across languages, the role of facial cues remains underexplored. This study investigated perceptual strategies for different facial regions in decoding Mandarin ironic speech. 44 native speakers completed a perception experiment including ironic blame and praise and their literal counterparts under Visual-only, Audiovisual (quiet), and Audiovisual (noise) conditions. Eye-tracking measured fixation duration and pupil dilation. Results showed distinct visual patterns: ironic blame elicited longer fixations on the eyes, with no pupil-size differences across regions, whereas ironic praise prompted greater attention to the mouth across modalities, with larger pupil size during eye fixations in the quiet audiovisual condition. These findings reveal asymmetric visual processing across irony types and inform multimodal intention recognition.

title: WaveNorm: A Low-Complexity Time-Domain Neural Adaptive Gain Control for Real-Time Speech Applications
authors: Deepika Ijjada(Meeami Technologies); Charan Kumar Reddy B(Meeami Technologies); Ashwini Hanaganti(Meeami Technologies); Priyanka Devrao Jadhav(Meeami Technologies); Varsha Uppalanchi(Meeami Technologies); Nivedita Chennupati(Meeami Technologies); Karunakar Reddy Pucchakayala(Meeami Technologies); Balaji Padmanaban(Meeami Technologies); Harish Rajamani(Meeami Technologies); Naveen Ambati(Meeami Technologies)
session_title: Speech Recognition, Enhancement and Real-Time Systems
abstract: We present WaveNorm AGC, a lightweight, low-latency neural Adaptive Gain Control(AGC) system for real-time speech normalization on edge devices. Operating in the time domain, it learns a content-aware, level-invariant gain mapping directly from raw waveforms. Unlike conventional rule-based AGC, it avoids fixed control parameters and hand-crafted envelope tracking, providing stable and responsive gain adjustment. WaveNorm AGC provides robust performance across a wide dynamic range upto -70 dB maintaining loudness compliance with ITU-T P.56 and P.79 standards under noisy conditions, while achieving ~6 dB noise reduction. The model is speaker-independent and highly efficient (49 M MACs, 55 KB of memory), making it suitable for real-time deployment on resource-constrained devices.

title: Listening with Attention: Entropy-Guided Explainability for Transformer-Based Audio Models
authors: Ravi Kumar(Florida International University); Utkarsh Grover(University of South Florida); Xiaomin Lin(University of South Florida); Agoritsa Polyzou(Florida International University)
abstract: Transformer-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) models such as Whisper are highly accurate, but their predictions remain difficult to interpret. Existing explainable AI (XAI) methods often lack faithfulness and precise temporal grounding. We propose Listening with Entropy-guided Attention for Faithful eXplainability (LEAF-X), a model-intrinsic XAI framework for transformer-based ASR. LEAF-X combines entropy-guided attention weighting, multi-layer attention rollout, and optional causal ablations to identify low-entropy, high-impact heads and layers, producing sparse token-to-frame attributions. Unlike perturbation-based explainers or raw attention maps, LEAF-X exploits the internal structure of encoder-decoder and speech-augmented decoder-only models to generate explanations that better reflect model computation. Results show that LEAF-X produces more faithful and stable attributions than strong baselines, supporting more transparent and auditable ASR.

title: Automated Measurement of Geniohyoid Muscle Thickness During Speech Using Deep Learning and UltrasoundAutomated Measurement of Geniohyoid Muscle Thickness During Speech Using Deep Learning and Ultrasound
authors: Alisher Myrgyyassov(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Bruce Xiao Wang(Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Yu Sun(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Shuming Huang(Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Zhen Song(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Min Ney Wong(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Yongping Zheng(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
abstract: Manual measurement of muscle morphology from ultrasound during speech is time-consuming and limits large-scale studies. We present SMMA, a fully automated framework combining deep learning segmentation with skeleton-based thickness quantification for analyzing geniohyoid (GH) muscle dynamics. Validation demonstrates near-human-level accuracy (Dice: 0.9037, MAE: 0.53 mm, r = 0.901). Application to Cantonese vowel production (N = 11) reveals systematic patterns: /a:/ shows significantly greater GH thickness (7.29 mm) than /i:/ (5.95 mm, p < 0.001, Cohen's d > 1.3), suggesting greater GH activation during the production of /a:/ than /i:/, consistent with its role in mandibular depression. Sex differences (5-8% greater in males) reflect anatomical scaling. SMMA achieves expert-validated accuracy while eliminating the need for manual annotation, enabling scalable investigations of speech motor control and objective assessment of speech/swallowing disorders.

title: SᴜTRA: Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness
authors: Vaibhav Rathore(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.; Indian Institute of Technology); Siddhant Gole(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.; Indian Institute of Technology); Dadhichi Telwadkar(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Rooshil Bhatia(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Maulik Ruparel(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Siddharth Surekha(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Neha Bhargava(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.)
abstract: Existing subword tokenizers optimize statistical compression but ignore morphological structure, particularly the relationship between roots and affixes. This is harmful for morphologically rich Indic languages, where basic units are complex orthographic syllables (aksharas) rather than letters. Frequency-based methods over-fragment words, arbitrarily splitting roots and affixes—a phenomenon we term Morphological Shattering. We propose SᴜTRA (Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness), a morphology-aware algorithm that preserves akshara indivisibility and penalizes merges crossing morphological boundaries. We also release a new morphological segmentation dataset for Hindi, Marathi, and Gujarati. SᴜTRA reduces shattering, achieving peak gains of +14.7% in morphological alignment (Boundary F1) and +34% in semantic recoverability (Hindi) over Bᴘᴇ. These structural gains yield an average improvement of +8.08 ᴄʜʀF2 in machine translation.
